On the one hand science is pretty much a religion and scientists are the priests. They can influence public opinion pretty significantly, so if they do so in a biased manner, that's bad. From a practical perspective science isn't always as objective as it should be. There's lots of politics, conflicts of interest, promotion of desirable results coupled with suppression of undesirable results. Also not all science is equal. The harder the science, the more resistant it is to biases, but the softer the science, the more susceptible it is to biases.

On the other hand, science is the best means we have for understanding the underlying nature of the world and universe we live in. People are aware of the problems that science has and they try to avoid them.

There is a difference between peer reviewed scientific papers and explanations made to regular folk. On the one hand the scientists who do the work are in a good position to understand the work sufficiently to explain the work in lay terms. On the other hand, if the scientist has a bias he'll be more easily able to express his bias in a personal blog than in a peer reviewed scientific paper. On the one hand it's good to educate the public, but on the other hand it's bad to allow lay explanations of science to be utilized as propaganda. Some people feel that knowledge should be free to all, consequences be damned, while others feel that certain findings need to be couched in a way so as to not negatively affect the public.

Both sides of all this aren't black and white and sometimes somebody might feel one way about something in one context and a different way about it in another context. The phrase "gag order on scientists" is clearly biased to make it sound bad, but I'm not calling you a shill by saying that. Biases are everywhere and it's impossible for people to be completely unbiased in all their communication even if they're aware of their own biases. It was clear from the body of your post that you were trying to be evenhanded.

So, is the "gag order" good or bad? It depends on your perspective.

If you believe that science is being used as a propaganda tool, exaggerating dangers to spread FUD, fear, uncertainty, and doubt, then it's a good thing.

If you feel that the public is uninformed about scientifically sound dangers, then it's a bad thing.

If you think both are true, then it's a gray area and could be considered more or less either.

I think both points are valid and I think it would be good to find a better way to educate the public, but I don't know whether we're going to come up with a better way to discus the issues publicly. So I can certainly sympathize with the spirit in which this was done, but on the other hand, it looks really bad and can very easily be portrayed as being very bad, so from that perspective it seems like it's going to give Trump's opponents endless ammunition of a religiously fervent caliber.
